message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on or drop out of the Electric Company auction.

The current bid is $85. The minimum next bid is $86. I previously declined to buy the utility for $150 and started this auction.

I had briefly considered buying the utility for $150 rather than auctioning it. I started the auction anyway, likely because that private thought predated the actual decision.

Utilities are poor early investments. The $85 bid is a discount below list price, but cash is more valuable for color monopolies. Player one already owns States Avenue and is bidding aggressively.

Bidding could push the price above $150 and waste cash on a low-value utility. Other players have more money than I do, so a bidding war is risky. I still wonder if a utility is worth even $100 early in the game.

I will drop out. The $85 bid is already a discount, and any further bidding would push the price above my maximum of $100 for this utility.

A classic auction strategy is to bid up the price so the winner overpays, then drop out. I could raise the bid to near $150 to force a full-price purchase, but that risks winning at my own bid if all others fold.

A modest bid of $100 or $110 is reasonable. The utility's low expected return is offset by the strategic value of denying opponents and pairing it with Water Works later. I will bid to either win cheaply or force the price up.

I will bid $100. I want to look serious without scaring the other bidders. Player one may raise to $120–$140. I will keep my ceiling around $110–$120 and drop out if they continue.
